title: Sleeping Beauty

story_parts.intro: Long ago, in a kingdom of rolling forested mountains, a wooden castle with tiled roofs stood above a valley. The king and queen welcomed a baby girl named Aurora. The whole kingdom celebrated with a lantern festival. In the courtyard, people bowed politely and shared mochi and sekihan. Gentle koto and flute music drifted through the air. Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather, the three guardian fairies, came to bless the child. They spoke kind wishes over Aurora and tied small paper charms to her cradle. But then a cold wind blew. Maleficent appeared, angry that she had not been invited. She pointed at the baby and laid a curse: before the sun set on Aurora's sixteenth birthday, Aurora would prick her finger on a spinning wheel spindle and fall into a deep, deep sleep. The fairies could not undo the curse, but they softened it. 'She will not die,' said Merryweather. 'She will sleep until true love's kiss wakes her.' The king and queen trembled, and the kingdom's lanterns seemed to dim.
story_parts.developpement: To keep Aurora safe, Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather took her far away to a secluded thatched minka farmhouse in a misty bamboo and cedar mountain valley. They raised her with warmth and care. They called her Briar Rose in the valley, but her true name was Aurora. She wore a simple kimono-style garment and helped with chores: sweeping the wooden floor, gathering herbs, and folding blankets by the hearth. The fairies tended a small garden and kept the hearth burning. They cooked simple meals of rice, pickles, and mountain vegetables. At bedtime, a soft lullaby floated through the farmhouse. Years passed like cherry blossoms and autumn maples. On the morning of Aurora's sixteenth birthday, while she was still fifteen for a few more hours, the curse found her. Aurora wandered to a quiet castle tower room and saw a traditional wooden spinning wheel. Curious, she touched the spindle. A sharp prick! Aurora fell into a deep sleep. When Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather found her, they knew the curse had come true. They laid her gently on a bed of petals and kept watch, their paper charms glowing softly.
story_parts.conclusion: Prince Phillip loved Aurora with all his heart. He rode through the dense, bramble-choked forest path lined with stone lanterns and tangled vines. Thorny branches blocked his way, but he pressed on with courage. Maleficent rose before him and transformed into a great serpentine dragon with glowing scales. Phillip battled the dragon, not with cruelty, but with brave heart and steady hand. Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather sent him courage and light. At last, Phillip defeated Maleficent, and the dark curse began to fade. He found Aurora in the quiet tower room, with the three fairies standing as guardians. He knelt beside her and gave her a tender, chaste kiss. Falling petals danced around them, and gentle koto and flute music filled the air. Aurora opened her eyes. True love's kiss had broken the curse. The kingdom lit its lanterns once more, and everyone celebrated with mochi, sekihan, and joyful bows. Aurora, Phillip, Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather lived with kindness and courage, and their love shone brighter than any darkness.
